Mitsubishi Chemical.desc: A Japanese chemicals group that reports five business segments: specialty materials, MMA and derivatives, basic materials and polymers, pharmaceuticals, and industrial gases. Sales revenue was about 3.33 trillion yen for the nine months to December 2024.

sources.title: Consolidated Financial Results for the Third Quarter of the Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2025 (Under IFRS)

Mitsui & Co. and Toshiba.desc: Mitsui & Co. is a diversified Japanese trading and investment company whose businesses include trading, LNG, iron ore, ammonia, food and healthcare; it had 53,602 employees and a profit of 1.1 trillion yen in the year to March 2024, with 125 offices in 61 countries. Toshiba is not described here because the sources opened did not cover it.

sources.title: Mitsui At a Glance (Integrated Report 2024)

Mitsui & Company.desc: A diversified Japanese trading and investment company whose businesses include trading, LNG, iron ore, ammonia, food and healthcare. It had 53,602 employees and a profit of 1.1 trillion yen in the year to March 2024, with 125 offices in 61 countries.

sources.title: Mitsui At a Glance (Integrated Report 2024)

Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited.desc: An oil producing company in Nigeria and the partner of the state Nigeria National Petroleum Corporation in the NNPC/MPN joint venture, which has operated in Akwa Ibom State since its first oil prospecting licence in 1961.

sources.title: NNPC/MPN JV - 55 years of delivering value to Akwa Ibom State

Mota-Engil.desc: A group whose main business is engineering and construction, reported in three regional units with further units in environment and in capital, Mext and energy. It works in Portugal and Spain, 14 African countries and five Latin American countries, and reported turnover of 5,951 million euros in 2024.

sources.title: Earnings Release FY2024

Mott MacDonald.desc: An engineering and management consultancy whose work spans transport, energy, water, defence and security, and buildings infrastructure. It is employee-owned, and reported gross revenue of 2.48 billion pounds for 2025 with about 20,000 people.

sources.title: Mott MacDonald reports solid performance in 2025 while enhancing employee ownership

Moulins Modernes du Mali (M3), Keita Gro.desc: Moulin Moderne du Mali (M3) is a food processing company based in Segou, central Mali, making wheat flour, pasta and wheat, millet and maize couscous, and recycling residues into livestock feed. Its annual capacity is about 55,000 tonnes of flour, 27,000 tonnes of pasta, 7,200 tonnes of couscous and 84,000 tonnes of animal feed, with 400 direct jobs, and the African Development Bank lent it 16 million dollars in 2014 to add seven production lines. The source opened did not describe the Keita Group.

sources.title: Mali: African Development Bank support improves livelihood of rural youth

Muriel Mining Corporation.desc: A mining company incorporated in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Goldplata Mining International, a Panamanian corporation owned by the Juilland family. Its Mande Norte project is nine concessions granted in February 2005 covering about 160 square kilometres in Antioquia and Choco, Colombia, for copper, gold, molybdenum and other minerals.

sources.title: Mande Norte mining project: English summary
sources.publisher: Comision Intereclesial de Justicia y Paz

Myanma Oil and Gas Enterprise.desc: Myanmar's state-owned oil and gas enterprise, sitting under the Ministry of Energy; the assets nationalised from the Burmah Oil Company were amalgamated into it after the 1962 nationalisation. It carried out the great majority of the country's oil exploration and production and takes a 15-25 percent share of production from offshore and onshore blocks.

sources.title: UKTI Burma - Oil and Gas Report

Myanmar Economic Corporation.desc: A Myanmar conglomerate set up in 1997 under the State-Owned Economic Enterprises Law to reduce the cost of producing basic supplies for the military, starting in heavy industry such as cement, steel and rubber and later moving into food and drink and financial services. Think tanks cited in this briefing say it remains fully within the control of the Ministry of Defence; in 2017 it was reported to own seven mining companies, 36 manufacturing facilities and at least three trade and service companies, with subsidiaries including Innwa Bank, MECtel and Ahlone International Port Terminal.

sources.title: Targeted Sanctions Briefer: UMEHL and MEC

Myanmar Mayflower Mining Enterprise Co.,.desc: A Myanmar mining company, named in the report as Mayflower Mining Enterprise Company Limited, registered in 2010 and based in Bangkok and Yangon, owned by the businessman U Kyaw Win, whose interests include mining, timber, banking and air travel. The Ministry of Mines granted it a 1,500-acre coal permit at Ban Chaung in March 2010 and added 600 acres in March 2012, for 2,100 acres in all.

sources.title: We Used to Fear Bullets, Now We Fear Bulldozers: Dirty Coal Mining by Military Cronies and Thai Companies, Ban Chaung, Dawei District

Myanmar Pongpipat Co. Ltd.desc: A Thai-owned company that operates the Heinda tin mine in Heinda district of Myanmar's Tanintharyi Region, under a large tin mine concession from the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry, formerly the Ministry of Mines. A villager quoted in the report said the mine began operating in 1999.

sources.title: Pongpipat follows Myanmar environmental regulations

Myanmar Wanbao Mining Copper (NORINCO su.desc: A copper mining company held, through Hong Kong Wanbao Mining Copper Limited, by Wanbao Mining Ltd, a Beijing-incorporated subsidiary of the Chinese state-owned China North Industries Corporation (NORINCO). It works the Letpadaung mine with the military-owned Union of Myanmar Economic Holdings Limited under a production sharing contract, modified in July 2013, that leaves 51% of profits to the Myanmar government through Mining Enterprise No. 1.

sources.title: Open for Business? Corporate Crime and Abuses at Myanmar Copper Mine

Myint Investment Group.note: Searched for the company by name alongside the Alpha Cement joint venture at Aung Thabyay and Mandalay; no credible page naming and describing the company could be opened, so left blank rather than guessed.

NCG Banco (Novagalicia).desc: A Spanish bank that had been through a state-supported restructuring. The European Commission approved its sale to the Banesco Group on 20 June 2014, finding the sale and the revised restructuring plan in line with EU state aid rules and facilitating an orderly resolution of the bank. The source opened does not use the name Novagalicia.

sources.title: State aid: Commission approves revised restructuring plan for NCG following sale to Banesco Group

NETGroup Solutions.desc: A South African consultancy to the electricity sector, founded in 1987, with divisions in engineering consulting, utility management consulting, energy and revenue management, and training, and about 234 employees. Shanduka Energy (Pty) Ltd held 30% of the group. The source names the firm NETGroup and NETGroup South Africa (Pty) Ltd rather than NETGroup Solutions.

sources.title: NETGroup organisation profile

NFC Africa Mining.desc: A copper producer that is the holding company of the Chambishi copper mine in Kalulushi district on Zambia's Copperbelt, established in March 1998 in the privatisation of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines. China Non-ferrous Metals Company Limited holds 85% and the state investment company ZCCM-IH holds 15%; it produced 68,757 tonnes of copper in 2023.

sources.title: NFC Africa Mining Plc (NFCA) extract from 2023 Annual Report

NHPC Limited / Narmada Hydroelectric Dev.desc: NHPC Limited is an Indian government hydropower company that plans, designs and builds hydroelectric projects and runs power stations, with 30 stations totalling 8,140.04 MW in operation in its May 2025 company brochure; it also has solar and wind projects. NHDC Limited is its joint venture with the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

sources.title: NHPC company brochure (May 2025)

NTPC Limited.desc: India's largest power conglomerate, generating electricity mainly from coal and also from hydro, renewable and nuclear sources, with further businesses in consultancy, power trading, training, rural electrification, ash utilisation and coal mining. The Government of India holds 51.10% of its equity, and it held 17% of India's total national capacity as of 31 March 2026.

sources.title: NTPC Overview

NVPSKG consortium (North West Water Inte.note: No credible page describing the NVPSKG consortium or its five named member firms could be opened within the search budget; left blank rather than guessed.

Nam Tha 1 Lao Power Co. Ltd..desc: The project company named in the developer's announcement for the 168 MW Nam Tha 1 hydropower station in Laos, which started commercial operation on 1 April 2019 under a build-operate-transfer arrangement with a four-year construction period and a 28-year operating period, after its three generators went into operation on 26 October 2018. China Southern Power Grid developed the station, its first international hydropower project, and Electricite du Laos co-founded it; the source opened gives no shareholdings.

sources.title: CSG's Nam Tha 1 hydropower station starts commercial operations
sources.publisher: China Southern Power Grid (via Land Matrix)

National Authority for Tunnels.desc: An Egyptian government agency, incorporated in 1983 and based in Cairo under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Transport, that executes metro line projects and does the relevant scientific and economic research, working with foreign and local companies. Its profile records more than 83 km of metro network built and project investments of 23 billion Egyptian pounds.

sources.title: National Authority for Tunnels (NAT) (Egypt)

National Irrigation Administration.desc: A Philippine government-owned and controlled corporation primarily responsible for irrigation development and management, created under Republic Act No. 3601 on 22 June 1963 and amended by Presidential Decree No. 552 in 1974 and Presidential Decree No. 1702 in 1980. Executive Order No. 69 of 2024 transferred it back to the Office of the President, after Executive Order No. 168 had transferred it to the Department of Agriculture in 2022.

sources.title: Annual Report (Consolidated Government Service Report)

National Irrigation Administration (NIA).desc: A Philippine government-owned and controlled corporation primarily responsible for irrigation development and management, created under Republic Act No. 3601 on 22 June 1963 and amended by Presidential Decree No. 552 in 1974 and Presidential Decree No. 1702 in 1980. Executive Order No. 69 of 2024 transferred it back to the Office of the President, after Executive Order No. 168 had transferred it to the Department of Agriculture in 2022.

sources.title: Annual Report (Consolidated Government Service Report)

Nepal Water and Energy Development Compa.desc: A Nepali power project company, the developer and borrower for the 216 MW Upper Trishuli 1 run-of-river hydropower plant on the Trishuli river about 70 km north of Kathmandu, a project costing 647 million dollars with estimated output of 1,427 GWh a year. Its shareholders are Korea South-East Power (50%), Daelim Industrial (15%), the International Finance Corporation (15%, acquired in 2013), Kyeryong Construction Industrial (10%) and a local partner, Bkesh Pradhanang (10%).

sources.title: Nepal Water and Energy Development - project detail

Neumann Kaffee Gruppe.desc: A coffee group active across the supply chain in export, import, farming, mill and warehouse operations, and specialties. Its own figures give 50 companies, a presence in 26 countries and more than 2,000 employees, with no year stated; the only dated figure on the page is a 2019 sales volume.

sources.title: NKG Facts & Figures

Nevsun Resources.desc: A mining company in copper, gold and zinc, with a Vancouver address, holding 60% of the copper-zinc Bisha mine in Eritrea, all of the Timok Upper Zone and 60.4% of the Timok Lower Zone in Serbia. China's Zijin Mining Group took up its shares from 28 December 2018 and was to hold about 92.44% after payment on 8 January 2019, then acquire the rest by compulsory acquisition and delist the shares from the Toronto and New York stock exchanges.

sources.title: Zijin Acquires An Additional 3.07% of Nevsun Shares

New Frontier Trading Corporation.note: Searched for the company by name alongside the Metales y Derivados smelter in Tijuana; no credible page describing the company itself could be opened within the search budget, so left blank rather than guessed.

Newcrest Mining.desc: An Australian mining company, listed on the ASX, TSX and PNGX under the ticker NCM. Newmont Corporation's scheme to acquire it became legally effective under Australian law on 18 October 2023, in a deal Newmont described as creating the world's premier gold and copper company, with closing then expected in early November 2023.

sources.title: Newmont CEO's Statement on Pending Acquisition of Newcrest Achieving Legal Effectiveness in Australia

Nexen.desc: An oil and gas company based in Calgary, Canada, with oil sands and shale gas in Canada and conventional crude oil in the North Sea and Gulf of Mexico. It was listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange until China's CNOOC Ltd bought it for 15.1 billion dollars in February 2013, after which it became a wholly owned CNOOC subsidiary.

sources.title: CNOOC completes acquisition of Nexen

Nidera.desc: A crop seeds business in corn, sunflower, sorghum, soybeans and wheat, concentrated in Argentina and Brazil with a network in neighbouring countries. Its owner, the Chinese grains trader COFCO International, agreed to sell the Nidera Seeds business to Syngenta in a deal announced in November 2017.

sources.title: Nidera Seeds, which operates mostly in Latin America, sold to Syngenta

Nien Hsing Textile.desc: A Taiwanese textile company, founded in 1986 and with its head office in Taipei. Its shares are listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange under the code 1451, listed since June 1993, and its market capitalisation was NT$4.298 billion at the share price of 15 November 2024.

sources.title: Nien Hsing Textile Co., Ltd. (TWSE:1451) company information

Nigerian Agip Oil Company (NAOC).desc: An onshore oil and gas exploration and production company that also generates power in Nigeria, and was a wholly owned subsidiary of the Italian energy group Eni. Nigeria's upstream regulator consented to Eni selling it to the Nigerian energy company Oando PLC in July 2024.

sources.title: Eni receives consent from Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission to the sale of NAOC to OANDO

Nippon Koei.desc: A Japanese engineering and design company, established in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo in 1946 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange from 1963, with projects in more than 160 countries and regions. Its group brochure gives about 6,700 staff and revenue of 198 billion yen without stating a year; the group moved to a holding company structure in July 2023 under Integrated Design & Engineering Holdings, established on 3 July 2023, and in 2025 it was delisted from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market and became a wholly owned subsidiary of Tokio Marine Holdings.

sources.title: ID&E company profile
sources.publisher: Integrated Design & Engineering Holdings Co., Ltd.

No. 2 Mining Enterprise (ME2).desc: A Myanmar state-owned enterprise reporting to the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation, responsible for mining, producing and marketing gold, platinum, tin, tungsten, molybdenum, niobium, columbium and heavy mineral ores. It has state, region and township offices and often works through joint ventures with private operators under production sharing contracts, holding both commercial and regulatory roles.

sources.title: Myanmar Mining Sector-Wide Impact Assessment: Legal and Policy Framework

Noranda.desc: A metals company whose reported operations covered copper, nickel, zinc and aluminium business units. It owned 59% of Falconbridge, raised that to 91% in May 2005 and to full ownership by 30 June 2005; shareholders of both companies approved the amalgamation on 30 June 2005, the amalgamated company continued under the name Falconbridge Limited, and it began trading on the Toronto and New York exchanges under new symbols on 6 July 2005.

sources.title: Falconbridge Ltd - Form 6-K (2005)

Norsudtimber.desc: A timber company, registered as Norsudtimber Aktiengesellschaft in Schaanwald, Liechtenstein, in 2006, that holds logging concessions in the Democratic Republic of Congo through subsidiaries including Sodefor, Forabola and La Forestiere du Lac. Global Witness reported it was controlled about 70% by Realwood Establishment (Liechtenstein), about 25% by Kreglinger International and 5% by the listed Swiss company Precious Woods, and that it held 20 concessions covering 43,426 square kilometres.

sources.title: Total Systems Failure

North-West Concession Company (Vinci).desc: Vinci is described in its own results release as a global player in concessions, energy and construction. Its consolidated revenue was 71.6 billion euros in 2024 and it reports 280,000 employees in more than 120 countries. The sources opened did not describe the North-West Concession Company itself.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Results

Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCI.desc: A government-owned Indian public sector company formed in 1987 under the Department of Atomic Energy, responsible for siting, designing, building, commissioning and operating nuclear power reactors. It runs 25 reactors with a combined installed capacity of 8,880 MW, as stated in its 2024-25 annual report.

sources.title: Annual Report 2024-25
sources.publisher: Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India

Nucor Corporation.desc: A steel maker and recycler incorporated in Delaware in 1958 and based in Charlotte, North Carolina, with mills, steel products and raw materials businesses; its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange as NUE. It had about 32,700 employees at 31 December 2024 and recycled about 18 million gross tons of scrap steel in 2024.

sources.title: Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024

OCP Ecuador S.A..desc: The project company, named in the article only as OCP, for the Oleoducto de Crudos Pesados, a 503 km heavy crude oil pipeline from Ecuador's Oriente basin to Balao near Esmeraldas on the Pacific coast, with a planned capacity of 450,000 barrels a day and the pipeline returning to the government after 20 years. Its sponsor group, which emerged towards the end of 1999, was Alberta Energy (30%), Pecom/Perez Companc (15%), Agip (7.5%), and Repsol YPF, Occidental, Tenco and Kerr-McGee with no percentages given; 900 million dollars of financing was closed with WestLB as arranger.

sources.title: OCP: maximum recourse

OMV.desc: An integrated energy, fuels and chemicals company based in Vienna, Austria, with chemicals, fuels and feedstock, and energy segments; its shares trade on the Vienna Stock Exchange. Group sales were 33.98 billion euros in 2024.

sources.title: OMV records Group Sales of EUR 34 bn with higher Operating Cash Flow in FY 2024

Occidental Petroleum (Oxy).desc: An international energy company with three segments: oil and gas, with production in the Permian and DJ basins, offshore in the Gulf of America, and in Oman, Algeria, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates; chemicals, through OxyChem, a North American manufacturer of basic chemicals and vinyls; and midstream and marketing. It is a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1986, with its head office in Houston, Texas, and shares on the New York Stock Exchange as OXY, and it had 13,323 employees at 31 December 2024.

sources.title: Occidental Petroleum Corporation Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024

OceanaGold Philippines Inc. (OceanaGold.desc: OceanaGold Corporation is a gold and copper producer running four mines: Haile in the United States, Didipio in the Philippines, and Macraes and Waihi in New Zealand; its shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (OGC) and OTCQX. It produced 488,800 ounces of gold and 12,300 tonnes of copper and had revenue of 1.29 billion dollars in 2024, and it floated its Philippine business, OceanaGold Philippines, in an initial public offering in 2024.

sources.title: OceanaGold Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Operating and Financial Results

Ocensa (Oleoducto Central S.A.).desc: A Colombian oil pipeline company. Its 830 km line runs from the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields in the Llanos basin to the Caribbean port of Covenas and has a capacity of 560,000 barrels a day.

sources.title: Oleoducto Central S.A. (Ocensa) company profile

Odebrecht.desc: A Brazilian construction conglomerate, renamed Novonor in December 2020, now a holding company for a group of six companies with about 25,000 employees. It employed about 180,000 people worldwide before 2014.

sources.title: Brazil's Odebrecht Changes Name After Years of Scandals

Office du Niger.desc: The Malian authority for the Office du Niger irrigation scheme, begun by the French administration in 1932 to supply cotton to French industry and to produce rice; cotton production ended in 1970 and the scheme focused on rice from the mid-1970s. After a restructuring in the mid-1980s its key services are water delivery, operation and maintenance of the infrastructure, land administration and agricultural extension; 60,000 hectares, 6% of the original target of about 1,000,000 hectares, had been developed.

sources.title: Making a Large Irrigation Scheme Work: A Case Study from Mali

Ok Tedi Mining Ltd.desc: A copper, gold and silver mining company that has worked the Mt Fubilan open pit in Western Province, Papua New Guinea, since 1984, with its registered office at Tabubil. At 31 December 2023 it was wholly Papua New Guinean owned: the state company Kumul Minerals Ok Tedi Ltd held 67% and Western Province entities the other 33%; it directly employed 2,741 people at the end of 2023.

sources.title: Ok Tedi Annual Review 2023

Okomu Oil Palm Company Plc.desc: A Nigerian company in the rubber and oil palm plantation industry, created in 1975 and privatised in 1990. Socfinaf, part of the Socfin group, held 633,172,832 of its shares, or 66.38%.

sources.title: Okomu Oil Palm Company PLC

Olam International (Olam Palm Gabon).desc: Olam Palm Gabon, established in 2011, has developed six oil palm plantations covering 63,330 hectares in Gabon and is a joint venture of Olam Global Holdings (60%) and the Republic of Gabon (40%). Olam Group Limited is a global agribusiness group listed on the Singapore Exchange.

sources.title: Olam Palm Gabon - Summary of Investment Information

Orezone Gold Corporation.desc: A gold producer that mines, develops and explores the Bombore gold mine in Burkina Faso, which reached commercial production from its oxide ore on 1 December 2022. Its shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ORE) and OTCQX (ORZCF).

sources.title: Orezone Provides Notice of 2024 Year-End Results and 2025 Guidance

Organisation pour la mise en valeur du f.desc: An intergovernmental organisation for the Senegal River, set up by a convention signed on 11 March 1972 in Nouakchott by Mali, Mauritania and Senegal, with Guinea joining in 2006, and with its headquarters in Dakar. It works on flow regulation and water sharing, irrigation, hydroelectric power, navigation, drinking water and environmental protection; the member states decided in 1974 on the principle of common ownership of certain works on the river, and agreements of 7 January 1997 set up SOGED and SOGEM to manage the Diama and Manantali dams.

sources.title: Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Senegal (OMVS)

Orissa Hydro Power Corporation (OHPC).desc: A hydroelectric generating company that is a Government of Odisha undertaking, incorporated under the Companies Act on 21 April 1995, which took over the state's hydropower assets (excluding Machhkund) on 1 April 1996. Its installed capacity was 1,272 MW at the time of transfer and is given as 2,099.8 MW at present on its own site, which names the company Odisha Hydro Power Corporation Limited.

sources.title: OHPC at a Glance

Otterlo Business Corporation (OBC).desc: A trophy hunting company, registered as a public limited company in Panama and registered in Tanzania as a foreign company on 23 December 1992 under the business name Royal Safaris Conservation Co L.L.C, with its registered address at the Mount Meru Hotel in Arusha. In 1992 the government, through the Ngorongoro District Council, granted the 1,500 square kilometre Loliondo Game Controlled Area as a hunting block to Mohamed Abdulrahim Al Ali, then deputy minister of defence of the United Arab Emirates and one of the company's directors; OBC started operating there in 1993.

sources.title: Business as Usual in Bloodied Land: Role of Businesses in Forced Evictions in Loliondo, Tanzania

Overseas Cambodian Investment Corporatio.desc: A private Cambodian property and infrastructure developer owned by the businessman Pung Kheav Se, who is named as its chairman. Its projects include turning Koh Pich (Diamond Island) in Phnom Penh into valuable real estate in the mid-2000s, the right it received in 2011 to invest in a 387-hectare expansion of the Chroy Changvar satellite city, planned to cost about 1.6 billion dollars, and the 2,600-hectare, 1.5-billion-dollar Techo International Airport.

sources.title: Developer of controversial Cambodian canal comes with baggage

Overseas Infrastructure Alliance.desc: An Indian infrastructure company, named in the article as Overseas Infrastructure Alliance Ltd, whose African work includes an electrification project in Mozambique's Gaza province, the expansion of an Ethiopian ethanol plant from 45,000 to 110,000 litres a day and an integrated sugar plant at Tendaho in Ethiopia. It has projects in Burkina Faso, Comoros, Ethiopia, Mozambique, the Republic of Congo, Rwanda, Tanzania and the Maldives, and said it had executed projects worth 1 billion dollars in eight African countries.

sources.title: India's Overseas Infra executes $1 bn of works in Africa

PATH.desc: An international non-profit, non-governmental organisation registered in the United States as a 501(c)(3) charity, working on vaccines, diagnostics, devices, disease management and health systems in Africa, Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Europe. Its total revenue was about 371 million dollars in 2024.

sources.title: 2024 financial summary, Annual Report 2024

PDVSA (Refineria Isla Curaçao B.V.).desc: PDVSA, written PdV in the source, is Venezuela's state-owned oil company. It held a long-term lease on the century-old Isla refinery in Curacao, which has a nameplate capacity of 335,000 barrels a day and whose normal throughput was around 220,000; the refinery is owned by the island government company RdK, and Curacao selected Saudi Aramco's US refining subsidiary Motiva Enterprises as preferred bidder to manage and operate it after the lease expires.

sources.title: PdV hopes to retain Curacao terminal, not refinery

POSCO Daewoo (Daewoo International).desc: A South Korean trading company founded in 1967 as Daewoo Industrial, part of the POSCO group since 2010. It was renamed POSCO Daewoo in 2016 and POSCO International in March 2019.

sources.title: POSCO Daewoo renamed as POSCO International

POSCO International.desc: A South Korean trading company founded in 1967 as Daewoo Industrial and part of the POSCO group since 2010. It was renamed POSCO Daewoo in 2016 and took its present name in March 2019.

sources.title: POSCO Daewoo renamed as POSCO International
